acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Corporate CEO Maurice "Morry" Taylor, Jr. was a Republican candidate for President, and he never had a chance to win the nomination. That didn't stop political reporter and author Michael Lewis from covering Morry's bizarre campaign. Lewis reads from his diaries about life on the road with Morry.
acts.title: The Grizz

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Jack Hitt reviews the strange case of William Kane, his mistress, his family, and fifteen vials of frozen sperm.
acts.title: Citizen Kane

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Michael Lewis continues readings from his diaries of Morry Taylor's Presidential campaign.
acts.title: A Candidate, A Voter, And A Room Full Of Pigs

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: The late Ron Brown, the former U.S. Secretary of Commerce, could have had an easy life, but chose instead to take on stressful, difficult tasks. Brian Gilmore, an attorney and a writer, talks about the collective eulogizing of Brown.
acts.title: Another Mixed Legacy
